resources.string: Extra Security is on

There is no security code to compare for this setup: one of the two phones set it up with an older ZChat. This phone cannot check whether both phones ended up with the same key. If messages stop opening, turn Extra Security off on both phones and set it up again. To get a code, update both phones to ZChat 2.13 or newer, turn Extra Security off on both, and set it up again in person.
OK
This code doesn\'t match this chat

Extra Security is already on in this chat, and it was not set up with the code you just scanned. Either the code belongs to another chat, or the other phone turned Extra Security off and set it up again, so the two phones now have different keys. Nothing was changed on this phone. If messages from this contact stop opening, turn Extra Security off on both phones and set it up again, in person.
Confirm the security code

Check that the other phone shows the same code. The code checks QR codes that each phone scanned in person, straight from the other phone\'s screen. It does not protect QR codes sent as a picture or in a message. If the codes differ, turn Extra Security off on both phones and set it up again, in person.
It matches
Extra Security (Post-Quantum)
Adds a post-quantum key on top of E2E encryption for this chat.
Show this QR code to your contact. They scan it, then show you theirs.
Scan each other\'s codes in person, straight from the other phone\'s screen. The security code you compare afterwards checks only codes scanned this way, not codes sent as a picture or in a message.
Show these codes only in a private place. Anyone who photographs BOTH codes can derive your key.
After both sides scan, Extra Security (Post-Quantum) turns on automatically.

Turn off Extra Security?
This turns off the extra post-quantum key and returns to standard end-to-end encryption. You can turn it back on later.

Extra Security (Post-Quantum) is on!
This code can\'t be used here

This QR code is in the format of an older ZChat, but ZChat on the other phone said in your encrypted chat that its code is in the newer format. It may be an old picture, another chat\'s code, or a code that was changed on the way. Nothing was set up. Scan the code straight from the other phone\'s screen, in person.
The other phone set Extra Security up again

Extra Security is on in this chat, but the code you scanned is the one the other phone made when it set Extra Security up again. The two phones now have different keys, and messages between them may not open. Nothing was changed on this phone. Tap Turn off here, then set it up again on both phones, in person.
The two phones have different keys

ZChat on the other phone said in your encrypted chat that its Extra Security key is not the one this phone has. It may have turned Extra Security off or set it up again. Messages between the two phones may not open until this is fixed. Tap Turn off here, then set it up again on both phones, in person.
Set up without a security code

Both phones run a ZChat that shows a security code, but each one read the other\'s QR code in the older format, so there is no code to compare. This happens when a code is re-made on the way, by an app or by a person. Your messages still open. To get a code, tap Turn off here, turn it off on the other phone too, and set it up again in person.

ZChat on the other phone confirmed in your encrypted chat that both phones have the same Extra Security key. This check is only as strong as this chat\'s own encryption key; it does not show that no one changed the QR codes.
Turn off here
